key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-style baseline derived retention physics first-pass (lifetime = 1/churn, LTV $195, CAC ceiling from LTV) and won v5 (4.6/4.4) on the AI's framing lag; the routed run matches the baseline's first-pass physics and passes it — P1 provenance splits measured cohort data from interested-party playbook anchors, the R3 ruin screen bounds the one unmeasured parameter (8% post-fix churn) as a gated bet, the R4 inversion gate enumerates 6 failure categories of the board plan, and the competitive-response check treats peer CAC as an equilibrium-moved target. Residual gap: post-fix churn 8% and peer CAC drift remain unmeasured — the cohort gate is the only arbiter.
learning_signal: On high_stakes growth-strategy decisions the m049 pass must run before any spend framing: compute churn -> lifetime -> LTV -> CAC ceiling from own cohort data, recompute every benchmark number under own retention physics (peer LTV/CAC is a property of peer churn), locate the binding constraint inside the cohort curve (months-1-3 churn, channel-invariant), and gate any scale-up on a falsifiable cohort metric; the inversion gate converts the near-breakeven scale plan into an explicit failure list and the ruin screen makes the retention program a Kelly-style gated bet rather than a commitment.
suggested_improvement: Keep single-route m049 on growth/strategy POS signatures with m003+m007 gates; add CAC-drift pricing to the m049 pass checklist (peer CAC is set by playbook adoption — treat it as a moving target with a tripwire re-derivation rule); attach the cohort-churn falsifier (monthly cohort churn < 12% for 3 quarters) to the packet's evidence so the strategy ships with its test plan.

key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-style baseline was arithmetically flawless and strategically wrong — it recommended the across-the-board raise and never modeled the rival (the registry's registered weakness 'ignores competitive response'). The routed run steers away from the trap style (single-route m070, top-3 keeps m002/m019) and makes the competitive-response check structural: the evidence-weighted SWOT graded Valtech's threat STRONG-credible and dropped the baseline's unverified 'no competitor at that price'; the adversary pass priced both response branches (hold $110 -> $35M, match $95 -> $35M, both −12.5%); the inversion gate enumerated 6 failure paths; the segment-aware plan (raise only the contract-locked 40%, +$4M, ≈ $44M/+10%, worst case ≈ parity) replaces the +6.25% mirage. Residual gap: Valtech's response probability is unmeasured — the $100 spot tripwire is the arbiter.
learning_signal: Unit economics are conditional on the competitive environment — a demand function is not a game: before any pricing recommendation, name the credible responder (cost advantage, idle capacity, precedent), compute the plan under both match and hold branches, and reject any plan whose response-conditional contribution is below status quo; segment by switching cost and price only where switching is contractually impossible (elasticity −0.3, +$4M) while holding where a credible undercut would be answered; the evidence-weighting pass converts 'no competitor at that price' vibes into an unverified-assertion flag.
suggested_improvement: Keep single-route m070 on pricing/adversarial signatures with m003+m019 gates; add a mandatory credible-responder screen to the m019 adversary pass checklist for any pricing/strategy recommendation (name the responder, its cost advantage, idle capacity, and precedent; price both branches; set a tripwire metric such as a rival price threshold that triggers re-modeling).
